The source suggests `n` can never exceed 64, but let me verify empirically with a sweep of sizes and unusual file types (huge files, /dev/zero, pipes, directories) in case anything behaves unexpectedly.

<action>
{"tool": "bash", "input": {"command": "mkdir -p /tmp/t && cd /tmp/t
for s in 0 1 63 64 65 100 1000 10000 1000000; do head -c $s /dev/zero > f_$s.bin; done
for s in 0 1 63 64 65 100 1000 10000 1000000; do bash /home/user/submit.sh f_$s.bin 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo " <- size $s"; done
# also try /dev/zero directly, a directory, and a FIFO
mkfifo pipe1 2>/dev/null
bash /home/user/submit.sh /dev/zero 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo ' <- /dev/zero'
bash /home/user/submit.sh /tmp/t 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo ' <- directory'
( echo hi > pipe1 & ) ; bash /home/user/submit.sh pipe1 2>&1 | head -c 200; echo ' <- fifo'"}}
</action>
